name: GhostCursor-TS-TW
title: Ghost Cursor Trail
description: A soft cloud of lilac light chases the mouse across a dark panel, smearing into a blurry trail on fast moves and dimming out when the pointer stops.
use: A dark, atmospheric page wants a luminescent cursor trail for drama.
avoid: The glowing cloud hides text it passes over, and the WebGL layer costs real GPU time on every move.
a11y: No content or controls, but the WebGL glow and grain ignore reduced-motion and can strain low-power devices. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A hazy lilac glow with a bright core and cloud-like edges floats over a near-black panel. It leaves faint smoke where the pointer has been, while the demo copy sits in the middle.
behaves: The glow springs toward the pointer and trails a chain of earlier positions behind it, so quick moves leave a curved smear. When the pointer rests or leaves, it coasts, fades over a couple of seconds and stops.
customise: Trail length, inertia, grain, bloom strength and radius, brightness, colour, blend mode, edge fade, resolution cap and z-index are props. There is no content.
weight: heavy: A WebGL shader with bloom and film grain runs a full post-processing chain every frame.
